items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Cully, Jack Butler and myself on trumpets... in Horace Henderson's band

ctx.x: he would be high and go to sleep in a chair until he became a little sober. We found out that his name was Charlie Barnet and that he was from a rich family. But it was some years later when Charlie took a band in to one of the big white hotels that I found out that he was a musician. He talked with us at the Strand but I don't remember him ever mentioning that he played sax. He really must have liked Neal's band because he came so often and spent his time in our dressing room.

Horace Henderson had a band playing in the Dunbar Palace which had been called Bamboo Inn when I first came to New York. It was a small dance hall on 7th Avenue between 139th and 140th Streets. He was using two trumpets, Gus McClung and Jack Butler, when he decided to add another trumpet. Gus left the band after Horace hired the other trumpet and I joined the band. The new guy was from Boston and was named Wendell Culy. Wendell was a first chair man with a beautiful tone and so much technique that Horace gave him…

The only musician in the band who had been with Horace in Wilburforce and at the Savoy was Talcot Reeves, the guitarist, and John Williams, ex-Scott altoist. The other men were new to me but I learned who they were in a short time. Cully, Jack Butler and myself on trumpets, Bob Carroll tenor, Rupert Cole and John Williams, altos, Sandy Williams, trombone, Talcot, guitar and Manzie Johnson, drums.
